actions.fyi: Nothing needed from you. The fix is built, measured and committed. One honest gap below, and I am closing it before I call this done.

content.label: It works, and here is the size of it
content.lead: Same yardstick, same six kinds of fog, before and after. Lower is closer to the truth.

rows: Dense fog now reaches the sky instead of leaving it looking clear
The lit haze overhead is roughly right rather than invented
Distance fades at the correct rate at every range
The air between you and the car carries the right amount of light

blocks.label: What is left is not fog
blocks.text: In three of those four measures the worst remaining error is now on the fog-free case — that is the air's own coarseness, with no fog in it at all. Fog itself contributes nothing measurable to the dimming any more.

content.label: How I know it is accuracy and not a different sky
content.lead: The easy way to fake this result is to change the answer and the yardstick together. Two guards stop that.

rows.title: The answer was frozen before a line of fog code moved
rows.note: Twelve reference values captured from the old code. They still hold, untouched, against the new code — so the fog lands where it always landed, it just gets there at real render settings now

rows.title: Switching fog off at its one source collapses every case onto clear air, exactly
rows.note: To the last digit, for all five kinds of fog. If anything else in the game were still quietly producing fog, it could not have

blocks.label: And the wider net
blocks.text: 122 tests across sky, cloud, exposure, reflections, shadows and lens. Everything that was green stayed green; the five failures were already failing and already have their own jobs.

blocks.label: Nothing in the game has ever rendered fog
blocks.text: There is no scene with fog switched on, and no way to switch it on from outside a scene file. Everything above is measured, none of it is a picture. That is also why there is no fog test and no fog reference image.

blocks.label: What I am doing about it
blocks.text: Adding the switch. It is small, and it unblocks three things at once: the cost measurement this job still owes you, the missing fog test, and the first pictures of fog you will actually get to look at.

blocks.label: One number still outstanding
blocks.text: What fog costs per frame. I will not have it until the switch exists, and I would rather tell you that than hand you a number measured on the wrong thing.

content.label: Found on the way, now owned

rows.title: A fog fault on the list was already fixed
rows.note: The sky's bounce off the ground ignored fog; earlier work fixed it. That job is dead on arrival

rows.title: The benchmark's own worked example does not work
rows.note: It names a switch that was never built, so that arm silently measures the control against itself and reports no difference

rows.title: The documentation checks grade the wrong copy of the files
rows.note: When work happens on a side branch — which is always — they read the main copy instead, so they report fixed problems and miss new ones

rows.title: The 250 m rule is not what it was filed as
rows.note: Fog is not hand-drawn near the camera, it is switched off entirely because the grid is too coarse there. This fix removes that reason

decisions.title: Build the exact fog first; re-measure; spread samples only if something is left over
decisions.why: Reverses the plan's stated order, where sample-spreading jumped the queue, and folds a third planned fix in for free. Approved 12 Aug.

decisions.title: The sample-spreading step is paused, not deleted
decisions.why: Its background reading is filed. If the re-measure shows anything left over, it is ready to build immediately.

decisions.title: How the exact fog combines with the air's own dimming over long distances is mine to design
decisions.why: The fog answer is exact for fog alone; the two have to be woven together along the same line of sight. This is the one genuinely unsolved piece.

decisions.title: There is no sunbeam feature — every light interacts with fog and air identically
decisions.why: Ruled 12 Aug and binding on everything downstream: no light may be shadowed in the fog while another is not, and a beam is not a feature, it is what a blocked glow looks like.

decisions.title: The fog's body privilege and the trackside lamps now have owners in the plan
decisions.why: Was written as 'the moon has no shadows'. It has them — the gap is that the fog asks the sun's slot regardless of which body is lighting the scene.

decisions.title: There is no sun and no moon — one kind of body, the same rules for everything
decisions.why: Ruled 12 Aug. Which body it is may be data — its disc, its phase, its colour — never a rule that gives one of them something the other cannot have.

decisions.title: The job is one way in for light, not a fix per kind of light
decisions.why: Ruled 12 Aug. Fog is handed the lights and applies one physics to all of them, so a source built later works by turning up — there is no separate job to add it.

decisions.title: Nothing places a celestial body by hand; the sky obeys the time and the coordinates
decisions.why: Ruled 12 Aug. A body's position is a result of when and where you are, never something you set. The hand-set sun and the switch that reaches it are deleted, so a scene, a test or a preset states a time and a place instead.

decisions.title: D3 is answered: fog is solved exactly over every stretch the render already walks, everywhere, with no exceptions
decisions.why: Dimming from two causes multiplies, so fog and air separate exactly: fog is the thin sharp one and gets solved outright, air is the smooth one and stays sampled. Revised 13 Aug on your call — the first version let the sky and the near air solve fog at different granularities, which would have broken an agreement at the horizon that is currently free. One rule, both paths, no seam to police.

decisions.title: Today's fog is frozen as the thing to be judged against, before anything changes
decisions.why: Otherwise the yardstick moves with the fix and passes whatever happens. This costs a morning and is the difference between a proof and a claim.

decisions.title: The two approximations the design leaves get measured, not argued
decisions.why: Both are small on paper. On paper is not a number, and this project does not ship one.

decisions.title: The sky's remaining glow error is accepted, and it is bounded by the render's coarseness rather than by fog
decisions.why: At its worst it sits beside a fog-free case that is already a fifth as wrong on the same settings, and it shrinks with render quality rather than needing more fog work. Chasing it means turning the sky's step count down, which is its own job with its own number.

decisions.title: Fog gets a switch that works outside a scene file, before the cost is measured
decisions.why: Fog can only be turned on by editing a scene file today, so it cannot be benchmarked, tested, or photographed. Measuring cost without it would mean measuring something adjacent and calling it fog.

next.if_nothing: I add the fog switch, take the cost number, get the first fog pictures in front of you, then have someone who did not write it review the change and land it.

steps.step: Add the switch that turns fog on from outside a scene file
Measure what fog costs per frame, and what it costs on a clear day
First pictures: the same place with fog on and off, near and far
Review by someone who did not write it, then land
Decide on sample-spreading from the measured number, not from the plan
